title: The Doghouse job with Eddie Johnson and Lester Santiago
summary: His first Bourbon Street job was at the Doghouse, with Eddie Johnson, Lester Santiago, Charlie Sylvester and Rico; the interviewers ask about Santiago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, I don't know, they sent, uh, uh, Morellis, he, he told me where to go and everything and I passed the test and all that. But I never did go there, I mean, I just stuck with that music, you know? Yeah. Then I started working on Boydman Street. Mm-hmm. Now, my first job that I could remember, first study job that I could remember on Boydman Street was at the, uh, at the doghouse. The doghouse was, is, matter of fact, uh, no, I don't think the, yeah, the building is still there. On Benville and Ramport. Yeah, I remember that part. Yeah, doghouse.

That's right. Mr. and Mrs. Martinez used to own a doghouse. Big fat woman, great big woman. And the man was a little bit of skinny man like that, man. Boy, that was a combination. And both of them used to get drunk. Boy, I didn't raise them saying anything. They raised more than the customers raised. Well, in that band, in that band, uh, I was playing trumpet. My brother-in-law, Eddie Johnson, was playing saxophone. My brother-in-law, Boynel Santiago. Did y'all know about Boynel? Oh, yeah. We know about him.
Lester told us a little bit about him. Lester, that's right.
Maybe you can tell him a bit more of him. Mm-hmm. Since you played with him. How he played.

Yeah, yeah, sure. I could tell him about Boynel. Matter of fact, I played with Boynel with learning a lot of these, uh, riffs and everything, you know? Yeah. Yeah. Well, at that particular job at the doghouse, I was playing trumpet. My brother-in-law, Eddie Johnson, was playing saxophone. Boynel Santiago was playing, uh, piano. Charlie Sylvester played drums.
